page.layout: One printed page with running text in one wide column. Short fragments of marginal notes stand in the left margin, cut off and stained red. At the right edge is the cropped edge of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: supra fidem verbis suis & purpuratorum suorum crepuisse: denunciasse, Graecos se non precariae & fictae, ab alieno pendenti arbitrio, sed verae ac solidae libertati, nixurae viribus propriis reddituram, dignitatemque pristinae restituturum: verum vanitatem statim, cum venisset in Europam Antiochus, esse dedectam, exercitus laceros adductos, pecuniam in Europa mutuo quaesitam, classes Romanis non pares, auxilii a Philippo nihil, nec Graecos aliove se commovisse. Itaque, ut discimus ex iil-dem[?] scriptoribus, Chalcis quidem in Euboea ab Antiocho, calente primo terrore, occupata, deinde varia tentata, [illegible, ~3 letters]tentata[?] mens non belli contra Romanos gerendi, sed controversias inter eos & Graecos ex aequo & bono amice componendi, etiam blanditiis & minis Graeci oppugnati, Annibalis, qui in partibus erat, consilia neglecta: Demum ad Thermopylas, quas copiis suis infe-erat, Antiochus ab Acilio Glabrione Romano consule, ingenti pugnā supe-tus & castris exutus, trepidā fugā Chalcidem repetiit, atque inde in Asiam rediit. Id turbavit quidem Aetolorum [illegible, ~3 letters]animos, sed non proftravit, nec infi-[?] ferociam fregit. Nam à consule [illegible, ~5 letters] store[?] moniti, qui Heracleam Thessali-

page.notes: Left margin: only fragments of marginal notes survive, cut off and stained red; they cannot be read and are marked illegible. Right edge: the neighbouring page is cropped and is not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "iil-dem" at the line end, the first letters of "tentata" overlapped by a margin note, "supe-tus" at the line end, "infi-" with the next word, the word after "Nam à consule", and the end of "Thessali-" with the catchword "lix". The paragraph is continued from the previous page.
